table_assessment.assessment_notes: Exact review confirms hospice, electrophysiology, referral, ICD, and biventricular-pacing instructions across two guideline versions. Version changes and a near-duplicate table in another source document require human adjudication.

entities.surface_form: Patients with HF undergoing end-of-life care
in the home, a hospital setting, or a special hospice unit

normative_assertions.notes: Hospice services may be considered for patients with HF undergoing end-of-life care.

source_grade_records.notes: Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.

text_units.verbatim_text: Patients with HF undergoing end-of-life care may be considered for hospice services that can be delivered in the home, a hospital setting, or a special hospice unit. (Strength of Evidence = C)

entities.surface_form: Patients with HF receiving end-of-life care
in the home, a nursing home, or a special hospice unit

normative_assertions.notes: Hospice enrollment should be considered for patients receiving end-of-life care.

source_grade_records.notes: Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.

text_units.verbatim_text: Patients with HF receiving end-of-life care should be considered for enrollment in hospice that can be delivered in the home, a nursing home, or a special hospice unit. (Strength of Evidence = C)

entities.surface_form: functional status and prognosis based on severity of underlying HF and comorbid conditions
LV dysfunction is a reason for recommending electrophysiologic intervention

normative_assertions.notes: The decision on electrophysiologic intervention should account for functional status, prognosis, HF severity, and comorbidity.
LV function should be reassessed after 3–6 months of optimal medical therapy when LV dysfunction motivates intervention.

source_grade_records.notes: Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.
Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.

text_units.verbatim_text: It is recommended that the decision to undertake electrophysiologic intervention be made in light of functional status and prognosis based on severity of underlying HF and comorbid conditions. If LV dysfunction is a reason for recommending electrophysiologic intervention, LV function should be re-assessed, ideally after 3–6 months of optimal medical therapy. (Strength of Evidence = C)

entities.surface_form: functional status and prognosis based on severity of underlying HF and comorbid conditions
an ICD is considered due to LV dysfunction which is of recent onset

normative_assertions.notes: The intervention decision, including ICD implantation, should account for functional status and prognosis.
Recent-onset LV dysfunction prompting ICD consideration should be reassessed after optimal medical therapy.

source_grade_records.notes: Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.
Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.

text_units.verbatim_text: It is recommended that the decision to undertake electrophysiologic intervention, including ICD implantation, be made in light of functional status and prognosis based on severity of underlying HF and comorbid conditions. If an ICD is considered due to LV dysfunction which is of recent onset, LV function should be reassessed, ideally after 3-6 months of optimal medical therapy. (Strength of Evidence = C)

entities.surface_form: patients with HF who present with syncope
In the absence of a clear identifiable noncardiac cause

normative_assertions.notes: Immediate evaluation is recommended for HF patients presenting with syncope.
Electrophysiologic referral is advised when no clear noncardiac cause exists.

source_grade_records.notes: Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.
Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.

text_units.verbatim_text: Immediate evaluation is recommended in patients with HF who present with syncope. In the absence of a clear identifiable noncardiac cause, patients should be referred for electrophysiologic evaluation. (Strength of Evidence = C)

In the absence of a clear identifiable noncardiac cause

normative_assertions.notes: Immediate evaluation is recommended for HF patients presenting with syncope.
EP-specialist consultation should be obtained absent a clear noncardiac cause.

source_grade_records.notes: Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.
Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.

text_units.verbatim_text: Immediate evaluation is recommended in patients with HF who present with syncope. In the absence of a clear identifiable noncardiac cause, consultation with an EP specialist should be obtained. (Strength of Evidence = C)

entities.surface_form: those with mild to moderate HF symptoms (NYHA II-III)
patients undergoing implantation of a biventricular pacing device

normative_assertions.notes: Prophylactic ICD placement should be considered at LVEF ≤30% for mild-to-moderate HF symptoms.
Prophylactic ICD placement may be considered at LVEF 31–35% for the same symptom group.
Concomitant ICD placement should be considered with biventricular pacing-device implantation.

source_grade_records.notes: Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.
Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.
Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.

text_units.verbatim_text: In patients with or without concomitant coronary artery disease (including a prior MI > 1 month ago): a) Prophylactic ICD placement should be considered (LVEF \leq 30\% ) and may be considered (LVEF 31–35%) for those with mild to moderate HF symptoms (NYHA II-III). (Strength of Evidence = A) See Recommendation 9.1 for additional criteria. b) Concomitant ICD placement should be considered in patients undergoing implantation of a biventricular pacing device according to the criteria in Recommendations 9.7–9.8. (Strength of Evidence = B) See Recommendation 9.1 for additional criteria.

entities.surface_form: patients with an LVEF \leq 35\% and mild to moderate HF symptoms
use of a device that provides defibrillation
patients who are undergoing implantation of a biventricular pacing device

normative_assertions.notes: Prophylactic ICD placement should be considered for ischemic etiology with LVEF ≤35% and mild-to-moderate symptoms.
The same consideration is graded separately for non-ischemic etiology.
A device providing defibrillation should be considered during biventricular pacing-device implantation.

source_grade_records.notes: Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.
Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.
Source-native evidence-strength grade preserved without cross-system normalization.

text_units.verbatim_text: a. Prophylactic ICD placement should be considered in patients with an LVEF \leq 35\% and mild to moderate HF symptoms: • Ischemic etiology (Strength of Evidence = A) • Non-ischemic etiology (Strength of Evidence = B) See Recommendation 9.1 for additional criteria. b. In patients who are undergoing implantation of a biventricular pacing device according to the criteria in recommendations 9.7-9.8, use of a device that provides defibrillation should be considered. (Strength of Evidence = B) See Recommendation 9.1 for additional criteria.

entities.surface_form: chronic, severe refractory HF when there is no reasonable expectation for improvement

entities.surface_form: chronic, severe refractory HF when there is no reasonable expectation for improvement
patients with a life expectancy of less than 1 year

text_units.verbatim_text: ICD placement is not recommended in chronic, severe refractory HF when there is no reasonable expectation for improvement or in patients with a life expectancy of less than 1 year. (Strength of Evidence = C)

text_units.verbatim_text: ICD implantation is recommended for survivors of cardiac arrest from ventricular fibrillation or hemodynamically unstable sustained ventricular tachycardia without evidence of acute MI or if the event occurs more than 48 hours after the onset of infarction in the absence of a recurrent ischemic event. text_units.verbatim_text: ICD implantation is recommended for survivors of cardiac arrest from ventricular fibrillation or hemodynamically unstable sustained VT that is not due to a transient, potentially reversible cause, such as acute MI. (Strength of Evidence = A)
